sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Smyrna, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Smyrna, in Rutherford County and part of the Nashville metro area, had an estimated 63,321 residents on July 1, 2025. That is 19.2% more than the 2020 base and far above the 39,974 counted in 2010. Its roughly 23 square miles take in a piece of Percy Priest Lake, and Stones River and Stewarts Creek are the main streams.

Smyrna began as a farming community, and its rail station between Nashville and Chattanooga made it important in the Civil War. Sewart Air Force Base opened in 1941, the first vehicle left the Nissan plant in 1983, and that plant now employs roughly 8,400 people according to Wikipedia. The Tennessee Army National Guard base and the Smyrna/Rutherford County Airport sit on land that once belonged to the air base.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Smyrna homeowners?
sections.html:
In QuickFacts, the 2020 to 2024 median value of an owner's home is $358,300, and owners live in 57.4% of the town's homes. Renters pay a median $1,461. The 20,226 households run to 2.79 people apiece, and the median household earns $81,926 (2024 dollars).

  • Foreign-born residents: 18.1%
  • Adults 25 and older with a four-year degree: 27.8%
  • Typical drive to work: 26.3 minutes
  • Residents under 18: 25.0%

The household size suggests a market of families, so bedroom count and yard space are worth leading with in a listing. Numbers are from Census QuickFacts for Smyrna.

sections.h2: How much property tax does a Smyrna house carry?
sections.html:
Smyrna taxpayers get a single bill from the Rutherford County Trustee that combines town and county levies. The table shows the rates the Trustee lists for 2025 and what they mean for a house at the Census median value.

Item2025 figure
Rutherford County rate$1.8762 per $100 assessed
Town of Smyrna rate$0.5257 per $100 assessed
Combined rate$2.4019 per $100 assessed
Assessed value of a $358,300 home (25%)$89,575
Estimated annual billabout $2,151

The combined rate and the bill estimate are calculated from the rates in the Trustee's FAQ. Your 2026 bill may carry a different rate, so read it for the figure the Trustee actually applied.

sections.h2: When does Smyrna property tax come due and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
The bill comes due on the first Monday of October and can be paid interest-free into late February. No early payment discount exists. Taxes cover January 1 through December 31, so a mid-year sale divides the bill by months owned.

According to the Trustee, a new owner should check the closing statement or ask the title company who pays, since unpaid tax stays on the parcel. When a lender escrows your tax, the bill you get is informational. Smyrna owners can pay at the Smyrna office, in Murfreesboro, online or by mail; the Smyrna counter is at 615-898-7705.

sections.h2: Can an older or disabled Smyrna owner get tax relief or a freeze?
sections.html:
Yes. The Comptroller's 2026 list shows a $54,690 standard freeze income limit for Rutherford County, and Smyrna is among the places that adopted the higher $63,470 local option. Filing closes 35 days after the delinquency date, in April.

A freeze holds the tax at the first approved year's amount, so a seller with one should alert the title company. To dispute a value, the county Board of Equalization sits from June 1, and a further appeal to the state board is due August 1 or 45 days after the county board's notice, whichever comes later.

sections.h2: Does Smyrna restrict short term rentals or repairs before a sale?
sections.html:
Smyrna's zoning ordinance bars renting a single detached dwelling, or any part of it, for less than three months. Once a tenant has stayed three months or more, later extensions can be shorter. The town may ask for the lease or agreement and can cite a violation after notice. A buyer who plans nightly stays will not find that route open.

Pre-sale repairs have their own rule. Homeowner permits are issued only where the owner lives, or plans to live, in the house. They are not issued when the work is for resale or lease, so a flip or a sale prep job needs a licensed contractor to pull the permit. The Building Safety Department at 315 S. Lowry Street handles permits, and additions or decks begin with a site plan sent to permits@townofsmyrna.org.

  • Interior remodels start with a pre-permit inspection, 615-355-5704.
  • Contractors need a state license, insurance proof and a town business tax license or release form.
  • A Certificate of Occupancy shows a structure passed inspection.

sections.h2: Is flood risk a factor in a Smyrna sale?
sections.html:
It can be. The Town Planner serves as Floodplain Administrator and the town posts FEMA flood map panels revised May 9, 2023. Zones starting with A or V are the high-risk areas, and a federally backed mortgage on such a property requires flood insurance. Zones B, C and X carry lower but real risk.

If your house sits near Stones River, Stewarts Creek or the lake shoreline, look up the panel before you list and have the zone ready for buyers. Any work in a floodplain needs a development permit from the Floodplain Administrator, reachable at (615) 355-5706, before it starts.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Rutherford County?
sections.html:
Rutherford County's register charges $5 a page, $10 at minimum, plus $2 for the computer fund. The state's conveyance tax adds $3.70 per $1,000 of price, which is about $1,326 on a $358,300 house.

Each deed has to carry the preparer's name and address. A title company normally handles filing, and the sale agreement decides which party pays the tax.

sections.h2: How is the Town of Smyrna governed, and where do I take questions?
sections.html:
Smyrna was first incorporated in 1869, lost its charter a few years later, and re-incorporated in 1915. In March 2000 the mayor and commissioners adopted a new charter, and the town now uses a city manager form of government in which the commissioners hire a manager to run daily operations. Town Hall is at 315 S. Lowry Street, which is also where permit applications are accepted in person.

For a sale, the questions split across two governments. Ask the town about permits, zoning and flood maps, and ask the Rutherford County Trustee, Assessor or Register of Deeds about the tax bill, the appraised value and the recorded deed.

sections.h2: Which way of selling suits a Smyrna house?
sections.html:
Listing suits a house that is ready to show. When a house needs work, has a tenant or faces a deadline, an as-is cash offer can close once title is clear, with no lender approval to wait on. Put the figure in writing and compare it with what a listing would net after commission, repairs and holding costs.

Whichever way you go, get a mortgage payoff figure, ask the town whether a property maintenance lien is open, and time the closing to your move so you are not carrying two homes.

faqs.q: Does a Smyrna seller get one tax bill or two?
faqs.a: One. The Rutherford County Trustee has collected the Town of Smyrna tax together with the county tax since October 2017, so a single bill covers both.

faqs.q: What is the Smyrna town property tax rate?
faqs.a: $0.5257 per $100 assessed for 2025, added to the county's $1.8762. Your latest bill shows the 2026 rates.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Smyrna house by the night?
faqs.a: Not under the current zoning ordinance, which bars renting a single detached dwelling to any tenant for under three months.

faqs.q: Can I pull a homeowner permit to fix up a house I am selling?
faqs.a: No. A homeowner permit is only for owners who live or plan to live in the house. Work done to resell it needs a licensed contractor to pull the permit.

faqs.q: Where do I get a flood zone answer for a Smyrna house?
faqs.a: Call the Town Planner at (615) 355-5706 or look up the FEMA panels on the town's site. Zone A or V property with a federally backed loan needs flood insurance.
